A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Direct Dependency Retrieval study. Their complete texts, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original dependency-retrieval and autoformalization experiments in Tables 2–3, with retrieval dispersion and multi-attempt analyses in Figures 3–5.

after.justification: V2 reports original hallucination, retrieval, and autoformalization results in Tables 2–5, with further multi-attempt results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The Qwen3-32B fine-tuning, dependency-name generation, suffix-array verification, and dependency-conditioned formalization pipeline are retained. Suffix Array Check names the existing verification procedure; the new integrations do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineLeanCorpus for Lean 4 dependency retrieval and statement autoformalization, retaining Diff01 through Diff89 and the MMA-trained baseline. The added analyses and model configurations use the existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: V1's retrieval comparison contains R@5, R@10, and DDR. V2 adds five prompt-based LLM retrievers to that comparison and evaluates no retrieval, prompt-based retrieval, and DDR within each general LLM in Table 5. These substantially expand comparator participation beyond the retained SFT baselines.

E3.justification: The reported retrieval-matching rule changes from component-suffix matching to substring plus component-sublist matching. V2 explicitly evaluates retrieval after hallucination filtering, drops F1, adds hallucination-rate evaluation and three-way retrieval controls, and replaces first-success distributions with intermediate pass@k curves. V2 specifies @8 for its autoformalization tables; v1 describes both @1 and @8 without identifying Table 3's budget.

E4.justification: V2 adds a quantitative hallucination study and weighted dependency-based difficulty analysis. V1's RA-focused multi-attempt analyses are replaced by comparisons across general LLMs: DeepSeek-R1 appears in the main text, with four additional models and repeated DeepSeek panels in Appendix A. The Diff01 examples themselves are retained.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 3 reports across-sample standard deviations for precision, recall, and F1; that reporting disappears. V2 instead reports hallucination-rate means and standard deviations in Table 2. Both retain eight generation attempts, without establishing additional training runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Many results are replaced: RA+DDR's Diff45 TypeC/BEq entries change from 0.60/0.59 in v1 Table 3 to 0.930/0.255 in v2 Table 4. Retrieval scores also change and F1 entries disappear. New results include ICL hallucination means of 0.21–0.39 versus 0.00–0.02 for DDR, plus the expanded LLM comparisons. Protocol and budget-reporting differences prevent interpreting the replacements as established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: V2 revises the identifier-match relation in Appendix C and introduces the explicit definition of hallucination rate in Section 4.3. These are limited mathematical-definition changes. The suffix-array construction and search-complexity reasoning remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V2 adds explicit core contributions concerning quantitative ICL hallucination assessment and dependency-based formalization-difficulty assessment. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion also emphasize DDR as a plug-and-play component for both SFT and ICL formalizers, broadening the contribution beyond v1's retrieval and RA-centered performance claims.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes hallucination-free retrieval from relevant retrieval and develops dependency statistics into an alternative difficulty indicator. Diff01 is explicitly excluded because imprecise descriptions defeat that indicator, extending v1's discussion of ICL versus SFT behavior. New limitations concern special constructs such as MOD and maintenance across library versions; the existing abbreviated-name and missing-metadata limitation remains.

D1.justification: New Appendix D supplies detailed dependency-retrieval and dependency-conditioned formalization prompts with examples. Appendix C adds exact model identifiers for Claude, GPT-4o, and Qwen-Max. Training hyperparameters and the dataset-access address are retained, while v1's explicit instruction to fill missing RA metadata fields with None is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds the GPT-4o system card and Qwen2 technical report. The related-work survey and principal contrast with selection-based retrieval largely persist, with additional positioning around hallucination assessment and alternatives to LLM difficulty graders.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten, and parts of the methodology are condensed. Detailed setup moves into Appendix C, the discussion is redistributed between results and a dedicated Limitations section, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded.

P2.justification: V2 transposes and expands the retrieval table, separates SFT and ICL results, adds a hallucination table, removes the retrieval-dispersion figure, and replaces the multi-attempt displays with new curves and appendix grids. Figures 1–2 and the examples are retained with relocation or caption changes. Typography and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: V1 tests DDR retrieval chiefly against R@5/R@10 and downstream integration with RA. V2 adds generative-retrieval comparators, controlled retrieval-strategy comparisons within five LLMs, and direct hallucination measurements, substantially strengthening evidence for DDR's usefulness beyond that setup. Prompt disclosure and specific limitations improve transparency. Retrieval-dispersion reporting is lost and cross-version score replacements remain insufficiently explained, but the stronger controlled evaluation provides a substantial net quality gain.
